_meta.title: Tunisian food composition table
_meta.why_this_exists: Couscous, lablabi, brik, ojja and mloukhia are absent from USDA FoodData Central, from Nutritionix, and from the fixed label sets of every commercial food-recognition API we surveyed. Without this table the device cannot cost a Tunisian meal at all, and the recogniser has no vocabulary in which to name one.
_meta.READ_THIS_BEFORE_CITING: Every composite-dish row below is an ESTIMATE computed by the team, not a laboratory measurement and not a database extract. Each was derived by decomposing a typical recipe into its ingredients, taking generic per-100 g values for those ingredients from standard food-composition references, and recombining them by mass fraction. Recipes vary enormously between households and between regions of Tunisia — the olive oil alone can move the energy figure by 30 %. Treat these as good-faith working numbers for a prototype, and say so in the report.

steps: Write down a typical recipe as mass fractions of its cooked components.
Take per-100 g energy, protein, carbohydrate and fat for each component from generic ingredient values (cooked chickpeas, cooked semolina, lamb stewing meat, olive oil, hen egg, and so on).
Combine by mass fraction to get the plated dish per 100 g.
Check the result against the Atwater factors (4 kcal/g protein, 4 kcal/g carbohydrate, 9 kcal/g fat). Every row below agrees with its own macros to within 1 %.
known_limitations: Ingredient values are generic, not Tunisian-specific. Tunisian lamb, olive oil and semolina may differ from the reference values used.

Absorbed frying oil is the single biggest uncertainty in the fried dishes (brik, fricasse, kafteji, bambalouni). We assumed typical absorption; actual values depend on oil temperature and frying time.
No moisture measurement was made. Stew water content drives the per-100 g figure directly and varies by cook.
Micronutrients, fibre and salt are out of scope for this prototype.
method.how_to_improve: Replace any row with a measured or published Tunisian value as one becomes available, set source.kind to 'literature' or 'measured', cite it, and set estimated to false. The test suite checks that every row carries a citation and that its macros stay Atwater-consistent, so an improved row cannot silently break the table.

fields.per_100g: kcal, protein_g, carbohydrate_g, fat_g — all per 100 g of the dish as served
fields.typical_portion_g: An estimated single serving, used only for sanity checks and for the app's manual-entry default. The device measures the real mass; this number is never used in a logged meal.
fields.estimated: true when the figures were derived rather than measured or taken from a published table. Currently true for every row.
fields.confidence: low | medium | high — the team's own confidence in the row, not a statistical interval

foods.description: Steamed semolina with lamb, carrot, potato, chickpeas and a red tomato-harissa sauce. The national dish; served in a mound with the meat and vegetables on top.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. Derived from a plated composition of 55 % cooked semolina, 20 % lamb stewing meat, 20 % cooked vegetables in sauce, 5 % olive oil, using generic per-100 g ingredient values.

foods.description: Coastal variant, typically with grouper or sea bream, quince and a lighter sauce. Leaner than the lamb version.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. As for the lamb couscous, substituting white fish for lamb at the same mass fraction.

foods.description: Chickpeas in a garlic-cumin broth poured over torn stale bread, finished with olive oil, harissa, capers, tuna and often a poached egg. Breakfast and winter street food.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. Bowl composition 40 % cooked chickpeas, 25 % bread, 25 % broth, 5 % olive oil, 5 % egg.

foods.description: A whole egg, tuna, parsley and onion folded into a malsouka sheet and deep-fried, eaten by hand while the yolk is still running.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. One brik as 25 % pastry, 45 % egg, 15 % tuna and aromatics, plus absorbed frying oil.

foods.note: Confidence is low because absorbed frying oil dominates the fat figure and was assumed rather than measured.

foods.description: Eggs broken into a simmering tomato and pepper sauce with harissa and sliced merguez sausage, served in the pan with bread.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. Pan composition 35 % egg, 45 % tomato-pepper sauce, 15 % merguez, 5 % olive oil.

foods.description: Powdered jute leaf cooked for hours with olive oil and beef or lamb into a near-black, glossy stew. Eaten with bread, traditionally at the start of the year.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 25 % beef, 60 % jute-leaf sauce, 15 % olive oil by mass in the finished stew.

foods.note: Confidence is low: the olive oil fraction in mloukhia is unusually high and varies widely by household. No published Tunisian value was found.

foods.description: Green-wheat freekeh simmered with lamb, tomato and parsley into a thin soup. A Ramadan staple.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. Soup composition 15 % cooked freekeh, 10 % lamb, 70 % broth and tomato, 5 % olive oil.

foods.description: Peppers, tomatoes, garlic and onion grilled over flame, peeled, chopped and dressed with olive oil, usually topped with tuna, egg and olives.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 70 % grilled vegetables, 10 % tuna, 8 % olive oil, 7 % egg, 5 % olives.

foods.description: Finely diced cucumber, tomato, onion and green pepper with olive oil, tuna, egg and olives. Raw, unlike mechouia.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 75 % raw vegetables, 10 % tuna, 7 % egg, 5 % olive oil, 3 % olives.

foods.description: Nothing like the Moroccan dish of the same name: a baked set omelette of eggs, grated cheese, shredded chicken or lamb, parsley and sometimes potato, cut into squares.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 50 % egg, 20 % chicken, 15 % cheese, 10 % potato and parsley, 5 % olive oil.

foods.note: Name collision with Moroccan tajine is a real recognition hazard — a vision model with a Western food prior will reach for the wrong dish entirely.

foods.description: Peppers, tomatoes, potato, pumpkin and egg each fried separately, then chopped together on the board with harissa. Street food, eaten with bread.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 80 % mixed fried vegetables, 15 % egg, plus absorbed frying oil.

foods.note: Confidence is low: everything in the dish is fried separately, so oil absorption is both high and highly variable.

foods.description: Green peas stewed with lamb, artichoke hearts and a light tomato sauce. A spring dish.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 35 % peas, 20 % lamb, 40 % sauce, 5 % olive oil.

foods.description: Beef or lamb liver slow-cooked with a heavy hand of cumin and garlic until the sauce is dark and thick.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 45 % liver, 45 % sauce, 10 % olive oil.

foods.description: A small deep-fried bread roll split and filled with tuna, potato, olives, egg and harissa. Sold everywhere, eaten standing up.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 45 % fried dough, 20 % potato, 15 % tuna, 10 % egg, 10 % olives and harissa.

foods.note: Confidence is low: the roll is deep-fried and oil absorption was assumed.

foods.description: Dried red chillies pounded with garlic, caraway, coriander and olive oil. A condiment, not a dish — logged in grams because a spoonful carries real energy.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 55 % rehydrated chilli, 35 % olive oil, 10 % garlic and spices.

foods.note: Typical portion is small but the device will weigh it accurately — this is a case where a 15 g measurement beats any photo estimate outright.

foods.description: Semolina dough filled with spiced date paste, cut into lozenges, deep-fried and dipped in honey. Dense and very sweet.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 45 % semolina dough, 35 % date paste, 10 % honey coating, plus absorbed frying oil.

foods.description: A ring of slack dough fried to order and handed over in paper under a heap of granulated sugar. Sidi Bou Saïd's contribution to breakfast.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 75 % fried dough, 15 % surface sugar, plus absorbed frying oil.

foods.note: Confidence is low: sugar is applied by hand and the coating mass varies by more than a factor of two.

foods.description: A dark pudding of ground Aleppo pine seed thickened with starch, layered with cream and dressed with nuts. Made for Mawlid.

source.citation: Team estimate, 2026-09-21. 40 % zgougou-and-starch base, 30 % sweetened cream, 20 % sugar, 10 % nut topping.

foods.note: Confidence is low: no per-100 g reference value for Aleppo pine seed (Pinus halepensis) was found, so its contribution was approximated from other pine nuts.
